mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is always active and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as a low rate environment supports equity valuations and reduces risk premiums.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals an economic slowdown that increases risk aversion and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 250, it signals an overheating economy and impending monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for the interaction of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns occur in < 40% of instances when the condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 255), the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: Rank IC for the regime condition as a predictor of 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns occur in < 40% of instances when the condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects strong economic activity and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1600 thousand units signals a strong housing market and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or positive returns occur in < 40% of instances when HOUST > 1600.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) rise above 1600 and residential sales (RSAFS) rise above 485000 million dollars, it signals a robust housing market and strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for the interaction of HOUST and RSAFS as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or positive returns occur in < 40% of instances when the condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by CPIAUCSL > 255 and UNRATE < 4.0%), the economy is overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to impending monetary tightening and recession risks.
failure_condition: Rank IC for the regime condition as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns occur in < 40% of instances when the condition is met.
